title: The mate of an isomorphism along equivalences is an isomorphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal C',\mathcal D'$ be categories, let
$L\dashv R$ be an adjunction with $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$
(unit $\eta$, counit $\varepsilon$), let $L'\dashv R'$ be an adjunction with
$L':\mathcal C'\to\mathcal D'$, $R':\mathcal D'\to\mathcal C'$ (unit $\eta'$, counit
$\varepsilon'$), let $G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ and $G':\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ be
functors, and let $\theta:L'G\xrightarrow{\sim}G'L$ be a natural isomorphism. Let

$$
 \alpha:GR\xrightarrow{\ \eta'GR\ }R'L'GR\xrightarrow{\ R'\theta R\ }R'G'LR
 \xrightarrow{\ R'G'\varepsilon\ }R'G'
$$

be the mate of $\theta$. If $G$ is an equivalence of categories (fully faithful and
essentially surjective) and $G'$ is fully faithful, then $\alpha$ is a natural
isomorphism.

(Proof to be written: for $c\in\mathcal C$, $d\in\mathcal D$ the composite bijection
$\operatorname{Hom}(Gc,GRd)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(c,Rd)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Lc,d)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G'Lc,G'd)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L'Gc,G'd)\cong
\operatorname{Hom}(Gc,R'G'd)$, built from full faithfulness of $G$ and $G'$, the two
adjunctions and $\theta_c$, is $\varphi\mapsto\alpha_d\circ\varphi$, by naturality of
$\theta$ and $\eta'$; since every object of $\mathcal C'$ is isomorphic to some $Gc$,
Yoneda gives that $\alpha_d$ is an isomorphism.)
